chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Shurayḥ, who said:

A man asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام while I was with him, and said: Damp cold and snow afflict us, and we want to perform wudu (ablution), but we find nothing except frozen water. So how should I perform wudu (ablution)? Should I rub my skin with it? He said: “Yes.”

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the Imam being asked for the ruling
key_terms.الدَّمَقُ: damp cold or chilling moisture affecting people in harsh weather

ai.seo_question: How should wudu (ablution) be performed if only frozen water is available?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a ruling concerning wudu (ablution) in severe cold when only frozen water is available. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام permits rubbing the frozen water upon the skin, indicating practical facilitation in ritual purity under difficult conditions.
